name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,426

clue.text: Piece of meat adheres to kitchen utensils

blocks.note: a chop is a cut of meat on the bone
something that adheres sticks

explanation.surface: A cut of meat clings to the pots and pans in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks are the pair of slender eating and cooking implements used in East Asian kitchens.

clue.text: Quack is briefly married to Bill

indicators.note: said briefly, the little word is cut down to its opening letter only

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
M is the standard abbreviation for married
a bill is a printed notice stuck up on a wall

explanation.surface: A charlatan doctor has just wed a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is the noun for a posted notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a fraud pretending to medical skill, so a person falsely claiming an identity or qualification.

clue.text: Dress made by name-dropping European ...

indicators.note: dropping a name means letting go of the abbreviation for name from the nationality

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
a person or thing from Finland

explanation.surface: An outfit worn by a social climber who keeps mentioning famous people, from somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Name-dropping is a social habit in the surface; here it means removing one N from FINNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a surface such as timber or stone is to give it a final finish or treatment.

clue.text: ... on tenterhooks since meeting head of Givenchy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: since, as in 'long since', means in the past
the opening letter of the fashion house's name

explanation.surface: Continuing from the dress clue: someone has been in suspense since meeting the boss of a Paris fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie this to the previous clue's dress for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog is being eagerly excited and in suspense, the same state as waiting anxiously.

clue.text: Rough tides drawn by tropical airflow

indicators.note: something rough is crude and disordered, so the letters lose their neat order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Choppy seas are being pulled along by the steady breezes of the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are the steady easterly winds blowing towards the equator across tropical oceans.

clue.text: Holy woman taking a new risk translated ancient language

indicators.note: the holy woman takes the rest in, enclosing it inside her own letters
translating changes a word's form, so these letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for a saint
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun takes a fresh gamble by translating an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the classical language of ancient India, used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Write to government about uninhabited Aegean island

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces sits around the next, wrapping it on both sides
with no inhabitants the inside is emptied, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: to pen is to write
G is the abbreviation for government
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A letter to the authorities about a deserted Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants an Aegean island, but Penang is Malaysian; Aegean only supplies its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is an island off the west coast of peninsular Malaysia.

clue.text: Muscle complaint

blocks.note: first meaning: brawn, physical strength
second meaning: a grievance or grumble

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a muscle injury; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang both for brawny strength and for a grudge or grievance someone airs.

clue.text: Fine example of smell associated with campanologist?

blocks.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bell-ringer might whimsically be called one who makes bells ding

explanation.surface: A prime specimen of the odour that hangs around bell-ringers.
explanation.walkthrough: A campanologist is a bell-ringer; the question mark flags the jokey invented word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is informal for an outstanding person or thing, a remarkable example of its kind.

clue.text: American insect seen round large tree ...

indicators.note: the insect goes round, enclosing the following piece within itself

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a familiar insect
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bug from the States is spotted circling a big tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Large looks like it describes the tree, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a tree with leaves silvery beneath.

clue.text: ... searching for quiet bird close to clearing

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a common garden bird
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Continuing from the tree: someone looks for a quiet bird near a woodland glade.
explanation.definitionFit: Probing is investigating closely, an exploratory hunt for something hidden or unknown.

clue.text: Stick found by officers next to river

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors, police officers
the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: Police discover a stick lying beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is a Welsh river; DI is the British abbreviation for a Detective Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: A distaff is the cleft stick on which wool or flax is held for spinning by hand.

clue.text: Tour leader getting skin problem from shrimp

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so just the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A tour guide catches a rash from eating seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrimp looks like seafood, but it is slang for a small person; titch is British informal for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for a very small or undersized person.

clue.text: Entitlement to drink is absolute!

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one
a right is something one is entitled to

explanation.surface: The right to a drink is beyond question!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitlement to drink' puts the right after the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright and absolute both mean complete or utter, as in a downright lie.

clue.text: Cast down to hell? Try to get close to Styx!

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld, and Dante's city of hell
a judge tries, or hears, a case
the last letter of the river's name is the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: Sent down into hell, a soul struggles to reach the river of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The close of Styx is X, read as the Roman numeral and written out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to make them dejected, the same as casting their spirits down.

clue.text: Other people holding roubles dare supply money to Soviet soldiers

indicators.note: the other people hold what follows inside their own word
read as the adverb of supple, the word bends freely into a new order

blocks.note: they means other people in general
R is the abbreviation for the Russian currency
the word rearranged
M is a standard abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Outsiders with roubles dare to fund the Soviet troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb about providing funds, but it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the name of the USSR's land forces from the revolution until 1946, so its men are Soviet troops.

clue.text: Doctor carried son into a protective environment

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are falsified into a new order

blocks.note: the four words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A physician carries a boy into a safe, sheltered place.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the person doing the carrying, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon sanitaire is a guarded barrier or buffer zone that keeps disease or danger out.

clue.text: Cereal product included in downbeat range of supermarket goods

indicators.note: the cereal is included, set inside the other letters
something beaten is battered out of shape, so those letters lose their order

blocks.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain
the first four letters, down, rearranged as signalled by the rest of the word

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal sits among a gloomy selection of shop products.
explanation.walkthrough: Downbeat reads as one word meaning gloomy; split it, and beat works on down.
explanation.definitionFit: Own-brand goods are products sold under the supermarket's own label rather than a maker's name.

clue.text: Conclude with penalty - essentially outrageous

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
the central three letters of the word

explanation.surface: Finishing with a penalty is, at heart, a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Conclude looks like 'finish', but it means to deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal is used informally for something annoying or outrageous, literally hellish.

clue.text: Little pieces of fibre blocking malfunctioning press

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, obstructing it
a machine that is malfunctioning has gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: lint is fluff made of tiny fibres
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: Bits of fluff are jamming a broken printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little pieces of fibre' looks like the whole definition; 'of fibre' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Splinters are small sharp fragments broken off something, so little pieces.

clue.text: Doctored mail about cocked-up surgery for tumour

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so these letters have been falsified into a new order
in a down clue, something cocked up is tipped upwards, so it reads from bottom to top
the mail goes about, surrounding the operation on both sides

blocks.note: the word rearranged
an op is an operation

explanation.surface: Falsified post concerning a botched operation to remove a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocked-up suggests botched, but in a down answer it turns the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipoma is a benign tumour made of fatty tissue.

clue.text: Mistake involving hook at end of line

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

blocks.note: a gaff is a hooked pole for landing fish
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An angler's error with the hook at the end of the fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing slip.

clue.text: Dwarf's bottom stuck between edges of gateway

indicators.note: stuck between two things means sitting inside them, enclosed on each side
the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the rump is the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A little man's backside is wedged in a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: Grumpy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy is the name of one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White story.

clue.text: Space used by South American president restricted by Republican ruler

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the president's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
Juan Peron was president of Argentina
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Room is taken up by a Latin American leader hemmed in by a republican monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Restricted by Republican looks like a container, but restricted only trims the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the head of an empire is a sovereign who governs it, like Napoleon or Hirohito.

clue.text: Start to embroider vintage fabric

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a cru is a wine vineyard or growth of a given vintage

explanation.surface: Begin stitching decoration onto old cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Vintage looks like it describes the fabric, but it is wine terminology.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is unbleached linen or similar cloth, and the pale beige colour named after it.

clue.text: Song about Queen attending animal's debut in part of zoo

indicators.note: the song goes about the next pieces, wrapping round them
a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter appears

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
QU is an abbreviation for queen
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tune about the Queen opening a new animal enclosure at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are tanks or buildings where fish and water creatures are kept, as in a zoo's aquarium house.

clue.text: Book of information having missing folio

indicators.note: having a thing missing means it is gone, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: facts are pieces of information
F is the abbreviation for folio

explanation.surface: A reference book with a page torn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Book here is a book of the Bible, the Acts of the Apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts is the New Testament book recounting the deeds of the apostles.

clue.text: Old person following recipe in Italian

indicators.note: following puts the old person after the recipe, so that pair is placed second

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
O is the abbreviation for old
a man is a person

explanation.surface: An elderly cook follows a recipe written in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Old person is read as two pieces, after the recipe abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman is a native of Rome, the Italian capital, so an Italian by birth.

clue.text: Mysterious substance emanating from a cop smelt terrible

indicators.note: something terrible is in an awful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the three words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A strange goo is oozing from a policeman who smelled awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the eerie substance spiritualists claimed oozed from a medium during a seance.
